title: Dutch Cape Colony
summary: In 1652 the Dutch East India Company sent three ships under Jan van Riebeeck to Table Bay to set up a supply station for ships bound for the East. It became the first permanent European settlement in southern Africa and later grew into a full colony.

uncertainty.note: SAHO's article says land was sighted 5 April and ships docked 6 April 1652; another SAHO page gives 8 April for the first landing.

where.historical_name: Table Bay, Cape of Good Hope, Dutch East India Company (VOC) outpost

importance.justification: First permanent European settlement in southern Africa, the start of colonial land dispossession of the Khoikhoi and San.

related.because: The VOC founded the outpost to supply its ships sailing between Europe and Asia.
